THE_SWEPT_AXIS.name: cell scale s
THE_SWEPT_AXIS.what_scales: the CELL inverter only: WP = 1.12*s um, WN = 0.74*s um, L = 0.13 um unchanged. The committed campaign-standard cell is s=1.
THE_SWEPT_AXIS.N_basis: the BEST N from Phase 1: the first N that crosses the 4.14 fJ/cell/op bar on the ideal-PWL floor row (4.1034 fJ/gate = 0.991x CMOS, measured N_min 59.5). Mandated by the brief.
THE_SWEPT_AXIS.SECOND_N_basis: PRE-STATED AND LOAD-BEARING. Phase 1's own measured numbers say the N=64 level time is HOP-BOUND with 65.93 ps of slack (t_hop 295.83 vs t_settle90 229.91), so at N=64 a faster cell CANNOT shorten the level even if it settled instantly. The settle/hop crossover sits between N=16 (settle-bound by 13.70 ps) and N=32 (hop-bound by 19.86 ps). N=8 is settle-bound by 24.17 ps and is therefore THE ONLY REGIME IN THE WHOLE ARCHITECTURE where a faster cell can buy level time. Running the scale sweep at N=64 alone would return 'no trade' without testing where the trade could have existed. Both N are swept; N=64 is the mandated headline, N=8 is the fair test of the lever.
THE_SWEPT_AXIS.PAT: committed PAT8 = [1,1,1,0,1,0,0,1] tiled N/8 times, HIGH fraction exactly 5/8 at both N. Phase 1 A11 MEASURED that a bank of identical cells on one lumped rail is a function of the HIGH COUNT only, so the arrangement is electrically irrelevant; inherited knowingly, and the VALUE and functional checks are still evaluated on all N nodes individually.

C_bank.why: the bank capacitance IS the cells' rail-side parasitics (pMOS source/drain junction area and overlap, both proportional to W). There is no explicit capacitor on rail{k} in this harness; C_bank_nominal is used ONLY to size the tank. Linear in s is the DERIVED expectation.
C_bank.label: DERIVED. The real secant C is MEASURED per row as Q_through_L/swing and reported as m_eff, exactly as Phase 1 A9 did (which found m_eff = 3.62..6.51 against a nominal 10, i.e. the committed 35.979 fF basis understates the charge that actually flows). Phase 2 does NOT retune the basis; it reports the drift so the axis stays comparable with Phase 1.

C_tank.why: holds the NOMINAL tank ratio, so the scale axis is not confounded by a simultaneous change of tank sizing rule. Falsified by control E2.

switch_width.rule: W(N,s) = 30 * sqrt(N/8) * sqrt(s) um nominal total, split tg15p
switch_width.why: constant-Q. Q = (1/R_tot)*sqrt(L/C). C grows as s at fixed L, so sqrt(L/C) falls as 1/sqrt(s); holding Q needs R_on ~ 1/sqrt(s), hence W ~ sqrt(s). Same argument Phase 1 used for W ~ sqrt(N), and the two compose: W ~ sqrt(N*s).
switch_width.note: Phase 1 MEASURED that this law OVER-SIZES by >=2x at N=32 (energy- and speed-optimal at 0.5x) and is about right at N=256. Carried unchanged so the scale axis is clean; W is not re-optimised per scale in the main series.
switch_width.convenience: W(64,s) = 84.85/120.0/169.71/240.0 um for s=1/2/4/8, of which the first three are exactly the N=64/128/256 widths Phase 1 already warmed.

t_hop.rule: PREDICTED to grow as sqrt(s) at fixed L, MEASURED per row by the true-ZCS probe. Never composed.

T_beat.rule: T(N,s) = ceil to 10 ps of (t_zcs_rise(bank 2, own probe) + 73.5 ps), Phase 1's committed rule.
T_beat.escalation: if a row fails B1 or B2 at that T, T is raised by 10% and re-probed, up to twice; the failures are reported as failures, never dropped.

max_timestep.rule: 0.25 * sqrt(N/8) ps -- Phase 1's value AT THAT N, NOT additionally scaled by s.
max_timestep.why: upsizing makes the CELLS faster while making the hop slower. Scaling the step with sqrt(s) as the hop lengthens would coarsen the grid exactly where the cell dynamics under test sharpen. Held at the finer value and the runtime is paid. Falsified at s=8 by B11.

CLOAD.rule: 2.0 fF per cell output, HELD FIXED at every scale in the main series.
CLOAD.why: CLOAD models the output node's WIRING/routing load, which does not scale with transistor width. The gate load that DOES scale is the next bank's transistors, and in this harness that is already structural (bank k's outputs are bank k+1's gates), so the co-scaling the crux asks about happens by construction. Holding CLOAD fixed is therefore the REAL CHAIN. Variant B of the crux experiment scales it, to separate the two mechanisms.

THE_CRUX_EXPERIMENT.question: in a real chain the driver AND its load both scale -- does t_settle fall at all, or is it scale-INVARIANT? Answer that before anything else.
THE_CRUX_EXPERIMENT.why_a_dedicated_instrument: in the 3-bank chain, t_settle is measured from the bank's own rail start and is therefore RAIL-DELIVERY-BOUND: the cells cannot reach 90% of rail until the resonant hop has delivered the rail. At N=64 Phase 1 MEASURED t_settle_after_hop = -65.93 ps, i.e. the gates are done 66 ps BEFORE the rail is. So the chain rows cannot isolate the cell's drive-into-load time; they can only show whether the LEVEL moves. Both are needed and they are different questions.
THE_CRUX_EXPERIMENT.deck: CELL_CHAIN: five identical inverters in series at a FIXED DC rail, stage 3 measured (so its input edge is cell-generated, not an ideal source, and its load is a real cell). Input to stage 1 is an ideal PWL step with the committed 2 ps edge -- a BOOKING, two stages upstream of the measurement.
THE_CRUX_EXPERIMENT.rails_why: 1.65 V is the nominal dV. 0.9422477 V is the MEASURED delivered rail of bank 2 at its own boundary in Phase 1's accepted N=64 row -- the bias the cells actually see. Two bias points so the answer is not an artefact of one.

variants.A_REAL_CHAIN: all five cells scale s, CLOAD = 2.0 fF fixed on every output. This is the configuration the main series runs.
variants.B_PURE_COSCALE: all five cells scale s, CLOAD = 2.0*s fF. Everything the driver sees scales. The theoretical scale-invariance test.
variants.C_FIXED_LOAD: stages 1-3 scale s, stages 4-5 stay at s=1, CLOAD = 2.0 fF fixed. Drive into a load that does NOT scale -- the naive '1/scale' expectation the brief names.

THE_CRUX_EXPERIMENT.metrics: (i) 50%-crossing stage delay stage2->stage3, both edges; (ii) t_settle90 of stage 3 referenced to the instant its INPUT crosses the fcrit trip, both edges; (iii) the fcrit functional-criterion time at the same fixed rail. All MEASURED from .prn/.mt0.
THE_CRUX_EXPERIMENT.decomposition_to_be_fitted: t(s) = a + b/s, from C_load = C_gate_next(~s) + C_wire(fixed) and I_drive ~ s, giving t ~ (a*s + C_wire)/(k*s) = a/k + C_wire/(k*s).
THE_CRUX_EXPERIMENT.B10_gate: variant A's t(s) must fit a + b/s with R^2 >= 0.98 on four points, and variant B must be flat within 5%, or the mechanism claim is NOT supported and will be withdrawn rather than asserted.

PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS_TO_BE_SCORED._rule: each is a falsifiable claim with a number or a band. Every one gets RIGHT / WRONG / NARROWLY-WRONG in README.md against the measurement, whichever way it goes.
PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS_TO_BE_SCORED.X1_CRUX_variant_A: t_settle does NOT fall as 1/s. It falls only by the FIXED-WIRING fraction of the load and then saturates. Quantitatively: t_settle(x8)/t_settle(x1) = 0.68-0.80 in variant A. Mechanism: C_load = C_gate_next(prop s) + C_wire(fixed), I_drive prop s, so t = a + b/s. At s=1 the x1 cell's gate load is ~3.7 fF (1.86 um total width x ~2.0 fF/um) against 2.0 fF of wiring, so the fixed fraction is ~35% and that is the whole prize.
PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS_TO_BE_SCORED.X2_CRUX_variant_B: with CLOAD also scaled, t_settle is FLAT within 5% across x1..x8 -- genuinely scale-INVARIANT. If this comes out flat, the area/power-for-speed trade DOES NOT EXIST at the cell level and must be stated plainly.
PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS_TO_BE_SCORED.X3_CRUX_variant_C: driving a load that does NOT scale, t_settle(x8)/t_settle(x1) = 0.15-0.30, i.e. roughly the naive 1/s. This row exists to prove the instrument CAN see a speed-up, so that variant A's flatness is a measurement and not a dead probe.
PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS_TO_BE_SCORED.X4_t_hop_at_N64: t_hop grows as sqrt(s), MEASURED exponent in s of 0.45-0.55. Absolute: 295.8 -> 410-425 -> 580-600 -> 820-850 ps for s=1/2/4/8.
PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS_TO_BE_SCORED.X5_LEVEL_TIME_at_N64: RISES monotonically with s, roughly as sqrt(s), because the level is already HOP-BOUND by 65.93 ps at s=1. x_CMOS_level goes 4.74 -> ~6.3-6.8 -> ~8.8-9.5 -> ~12.2-13.2. NO speed win at N=64 at any scale.
PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS_TO_BE_SCORED.X6_ENERGY_at_N64: E/gate RISES roughly LINEARLY in s. E_tank_loss ~ C_bank ~ s at constant Q, and the switch drive ~ W ~ sqrt(s). On the ideal-PWL floor row: 4.103 fJ/gate at s=1 -> 7.5-8.8 at s=2 -> 14-18 at s=4 -> 27-36 at s=8. CONSEQUENCE: the crossing Phase 1 found at N=64 (0.991x) is DESTROYED by any upsizing; x_CMOS ~= s.
PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS_TO_BE_SCORED.X7_AREA_at_N64: tank um2/gate = 29.98*s exactly by construction (C_tank ~ s); cell active area/gate = 0.242*s um2; switch active/gate ~ sqrt(s). So area rises linearly in s while speed FALLS as sqrt(s) and energy rises as s.
PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS_TO_BE_SCORED.X8_THE_LEVER_AT_N8_the_fair_test: EVEN AT N=8, WHERE THE LEVEL IS SETTLE-BOUND, UPSIZING DOES NOT SHORTEN THE LEVEL. The settle slack at N=8 is only 24.17 ps (t_settle90 150.72 vs t_hop 126.55), and s=2 alone adds sqrt(2)-1 = 41% to the hop = +52 ps, which already exceeds the entire slack. So the level time is minimised at s=1 at EVERY N, and there is no (N,s) in this architecture where upsizing buys speed. Predicted N=8 level times: 150.7(s=1, settle-bound) -> ~179(s=2, now hop-bound) -> ~253(s=4) -> ~358(s=8).
PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS_TO_BE_SCORED.X9_THE_MECHANISM_THAT_DEFEATS_THE_LEVER: THE CELL'S LOAD AND THE BANK'S RESONANT TANK ARE THE SAME CAPACITANCE. In CMOS, upsizing a gate pays for itself in the NEXT stage's load, a local and linear cost, and the speed-up is real. In QAL, upsizing pays into the LC hop that charges the whole bank, and the hop is pi*sqrt(LC), so a factor s of cell width costs sqrt(s) on the ENTIRE LEVEL while buying back only the fixed-wiring fraction of one cell's settling. The lever is not merely weak, it is structurally inverted: the thing you must grow to go faster is the thing that sets the speed limit.
PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS_TO_BE_SCORED.X10_ISO_HOP_EXTENSION: the obvious rescue -- drop L as 1/s to hold t_hop constant -- is WORSE, not better. At L ~ 1/s: I_pk ~ s, so series-R loss ~ I^2*R*t ~ s^2 at fixed t_hop; and Q = (1/R)*sqrt(L/C) falls as 1/s with R_S pinned at 10 ohm, so the fractional resonant loss pi/Q RISES as s and E/gate ~ s^2. Predicted at N=64 s=4, L=3.75 nH: t_hop within 10% of 295.8 ps, and E/gate 45-90 fJ, i.e. 11-22x CMOS. So the speed can be bought back with L, and the price is quadratic -- a NEGATIVE exchange rate against the sqrt(s)-hop baseline.
PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS_TO_BE_SCORED.X11_EXCHANGE_RATE: there will be NO positive exchange rate on this axis. Predicted signature: every scale point is worse than s=1 on BOTH energy and speed simultaneously, so the 'curve' is not a frontier but a single dominated ray. If instead any point beats s=1 on level time, X8/X9 are WRONG and the trade exists -- that is the falsification and it will be reported as a major positive result if it fires.
PRE_STATED_EXPECTATIONS_TO_BE_SCORED.X12_WHAT_WOULD_FALSIFY_THE_MECHANISM: (i) variant A t(x8)/t(x1) < 0.5 would mean the load does not co-scale as claimed; (ii) variant B not flat would mean the decomposition is wrong; (iii) any level time at any (N,s>1) below the s=1 level time at the same N would mean the lever exists.

BOOKINGS_ideal_sources_every_one_a_BOUND.1_buck: the converter that must resupply the tank loss is NOT simulated. Declared here, before the first deck, with the reason: the fixed buck sequencing is embodied in the gate PWL, but no switching converter is in the loop. Every energy row is therefore a BOUND on a complete system, not a measurement of one.
BOOKINGS_ideal_sources_every_one_a_BOUND.2_timer: not simulated. Reported at 0 (a strict BOUND) and at the campaign's 3.5227 fJ ideal-PWL floor (ASSUMED).
BOOKINGS_ideal_sources_every_one_a_BOUND.3_gate_drive_idealPWL: the switch gate drive is PWL voltage sources. Phase 1 MEASURED that this integrator goes NEGATIVE (the sources RECEIVE energy, -0.30 to -10.21 fJ/bank), so the floor row is SUBSIDISED -- a perfectly recovering driver nets zero, not negative. Expected to worsen with s since W ~ sqrt(s). Reported per row.
BOOKINGS_ideal_sources_every_one_a_BOUND.4_well_rail: the pMOS well rail (VHI) draws negative energy and is uncharged under the committed ideal-rails convention. Phase 1 measured -38.87 fJ/bank at N=64 s=1 = 0.607 fJ/gate, and charging it ERASES the Phase 1 crossing (4.711 fJ/gate = 1.138x). Reported at every scale, and the 'well-charged' variant is carried as a named column.
BOOKINGS_ideal_sources_every_one_a_BOUND.5_bank1_inputs: bank 1's N inputs are ideal DC sources.
BOOKINGS_ideal_sources_every_one_a_BOUND.6_crux_input_step: the CELL_CHAIN input is an ideal 2 ps PWL edge, two stages upstream of the measured stage.
BOOKINGS_ideal_sources_every_one_a_BOUND.7_JUNCAP200_leakage: LOWER bounds only: the shim's default PD = 1.00 um is smaller than the 1.12 um pMOS, so the STI-edge term clips to zero. Worse at s>1, where the drawn width is 2.24-8.96 um against the same 1.00 um default.
BOOKINGS_ideal_sources_every_one_a_BOUND.8_area: DERIVED from MIM 1.5 fF/um^2 and drawn width x 0.13 um channel length. Not laid out. The ONE 15 nH inductor per bank is NOT area-modelled and the committed record calls it the architecture's largest and scarcest component.

CONTROLS_AND_EXTENSIONS.E1_load_not_scaled_in_the_CHAIN: N=64, s=4 on banks 1-2 with bank 3 left at s=1, so the measured bank drives an UNSCALED load inside the real chain. Separates 'the cell got faster' from 'the load grew with it' where it actually matters. Pre-stated signature: bank 2's settling improves relative to the all-s=4 row, and the level time still does not, because the hop is set by bank 2's own tank.
CONTROLS_AND_EXTENSIONS.E2_tank_sized_from_MEASURED_C: N=64, s=4 with C_tank set from the MEASURED secant C_bank at s=4 rather than the nominal, holding m_eff at its s=1 value. Falsifies the C_tank sizing rule as a confound.
CONTROLS_AND_EXTENSIONS.E3_ISO_HOP: N=64, s=4 with L = 15/4 = 3.75 nH, holding t_hop at its s=1 value. Tests X10. Clearly labelled an EXTENSION beyond the brief's fixed-L configuration and never folded into the main series.
CONTROLS_AND_EXTENSIONS.E4_HALF_STEP: N=64, s=8 at half the pre-registered max step. B11.
CONTROLS_AND_EXTENSIONS.E5_s16: if and only if the s=1..8 trend is ambiguous, one s=16 point at N=64. Not planned; recorded so that running it is not a silent addition.

LABELLING_DISCIPLINE: every reported quantity carries MEASURED, DERIVED or ASSUMED. Anything modelled as an ideal source is a BOOKING and its row is a BOUND. A single-cell or single-hop number is NEVER quoted as a chain result, and the tank-only energy is NEVER quoted as the block energy. If upsizing delivers the promise that is a major positive result and it will be stated as clearly as the negatives; if it does not, the MECHANISM that defeats it is the deliverable.
